clue.text: Violent end

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as a grim phrase about a death, but each is a separate meaning of one word, first an adjective and then a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as an adjective for something severe or drastic and as a noun for the outermost limit of anything.

clue.text: The thing is, some spent it yesterday

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run taken from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of spent, all of it, and the start of yesterday

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that a sum of money has already been spent, all of it yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The thing is' reads like a conversational opener, but 'The thing' is the definition and 'is' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An entity is any existing object or being considered in its own right, a general word for a thing.

clue.text: Taking turn in vehicle leading to a stressful experience

indicators.note: a vehicle taking something in holds it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle on rails
as in a U-turn
taken as written

explanation.surface: A passenger whose bus swerves round a corner finds the ride nerve-racking.
explanation.walkthrough: The U goes inside TRAM to make TRAUM, which then leads to A.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is a deeply distressing or disturbing experience, or the emotional shock that follows one.

clue.text: Explained complex day

parts.note: elaborate means intricate or complicated
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone recounts how the day was complicated to describe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex day' looks like a noun phrase, but 'complex' is an adjective giving one piece and 'day' an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate is to add detail to a statement, so having elaborated a point is having explained it more fully.

clue.text: Clubber lost his head in aftermath of fire

indicators.note: losing a head means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a clubber here is a member of a club, not a nightclub-goer

explanation.surface: A clubgoer in a blaze suffers a gruesome fate amid the smouldering ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubber' suggests a nightclub-goer or someone wielding a club; it means one who belongs to a club. Drop the M from MEMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a glowing fragment of coal or wood left smouldering once a fire has died down.

clue.text: Old soldier in Japan knocks back rum in Asia, drunkenly

indicators.note: knocking back a drink suggests tipping it backwards, so the word is read from its end
one piece is placed in the middle of the other
a drunk staggers about out of line, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A veteran warrior in Japan downs rum somewhere in Asia while staggering about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocks back' reads as drinking the rum, which suits the surface, but it is the signal to turn the word round before it goes inside the jumbled continent.
explanation.definitionFit: The samurai were the hereditary warrior class of feudal Japan, abolished in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Pre-match ritual

parts.note: surface reading: a team's warm-up or superstition before a football game
setter's reading: the match is a marriage, and the ritual is the groom's party with his friends before the wedding

explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' pulls toward sport, but a match is also a marriage. A stag night is the British name for a bachelor party.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag night is a celebration held for a man by his male friends shortly before his wedding, a customary rite.

clue.text: Fashion brand

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to form or construct something, used as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion brand' reads as a clothing label, but 'Fashion' is a verb and 'brand' a separate noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb meaning to create or shape and as a noun for the manufacturer or trade name of a product.

clue.text: Feedback after moving into care

indicators.note: things that are moving shift position, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Comments received once an elderly relative has been settled in a care home.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is a response to something, and feedback is the response people give to an action or product.

clue.text: Single out endless lack of activity

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: letters put out of place are disordered, so this word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, not as an instruction to remove a letter

explanation.surface: A complaint that one person is singled out for constant laziness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' looks like a deletion signal, but here it is the whole word to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is the state of not working or doing anything, which is simply an absence of activity.

clue.text: Woman without one piece of jewellery

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word sits around the other

parts.note: a woman's first name
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A woman who goes without a single item of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' seems to mean lacking, but it is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head, especially by women on formal occasions.

clue.text: Deficiency in second-class post amounts to a crime

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: B grade is second class, after A
a lack is a shortage
post and mail are both letters delivered

explanation.surface: Failings in the second-class postal service are so bad they amount to a criminal offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-class post' reads as one phrase, but 'second-class' gives a grade letter and 'post' a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackmail is the offence of demanding money or favours by threatening to reveal damaging information.

clue.text: Miner about to play instrument

indicators.note: letters set to play move about freely, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A coal miner is about to perform on a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' belongs to the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambourine is a small hand drum with jingling metal discs set in its frame, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: The way one casually has to impress?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
'un is the informal spoken form of one, as in a good 'un

explanation.surface: A question about how someone speaking casually must behave to make an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One casually' signals the slangy 'un for one.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish or overwhelm someone, an intense way of impressing them.

clue.text: Denial of outstanding charge one added on

indicators.note: pieces added to one another are joined end to end

parts.note: a star performer is outstanding
value added tax, a charge on goods in Britain
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to pay an unpaid bill with a surcharge added on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding charge' looks like an unpaid bill, but the words give separate pieces. VAT is value added tax, Britain's sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Starvation is being deprived of food, so it is a denial of nourishment; the definition is loose but fair.

clue.text: Claims a student put to embassies

indicators.note: one thing put to another is placed right up against it

parts.note: taken as written
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
a legation is a diplomatic mission, a minor embassy

explanation.surface: Accusations a student makes to foreign embassies.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegations are assertions made without proof, and claims are statements that something is so.

clue.text: Example of cutting-edge green technology

parts.note: surface reading: an advanced eco-friendly invention
setter's reading: a machine with a literal cutting edge that is used on the green grass of a garden

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting-edge' and 'green' suggest innovation and environmentalism; read literally, they describe blades and grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden machine with rotating blades that trims grass, so it cuts and is used on green turf.

clue.text: Flower border at water's lowest point

parts.note: a river is something that flows, a flow-er
a flower bed or border in a garden

explanation.surface: A gardener's flower border placed down by the water's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means a thing that flows, not a bloom, a standard crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A riverbed is the channel floor over which a river runs, the bottom of the water.

clue.text: Married off along with one's latest suitors

indicators.note: something gone off has gone wrong, so these letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the latest of a word is its very final letter

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Once someone is married, the would-be partners all disappear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Married off' reads as a phrase about a wedding, but 'off' is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitors are people courting someone, and admirers likewise are those romantically attracted to a person.

clue.text: Beset by difficulty when we detain rep illegally

indicators.note: acting illegally means not by the rules, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: We land in trouble after unlawfully holding a sales representative.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in deep water is an idiom for being in serious trouble, as if out of one's depth.

clue.text: Repeated prayer curtailed serious hazard

indicators.note: to curtail is to cut short, so the tail end of the word is removed

parts.note: a man-trap is a hidden trap set to catch trespassers

explanation.surface: A prayer cut short because of some grave danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtailed' seems to describe the prayer, but it acts on the hazard that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase chanted again and again in meditation or worship.

clue.text: It's likely to carry one off in the end

definitions.text: It's likely to carry one off in the end

parts.words: It's likely to carry one off in the end
parts.note: surface reading: something, such as a disease, that will eventually kill a person

parts.words: It's likely to carry one off in the end
parts.note: setter's reading: the vehicle that literally carries a person away at the end of life

explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry off' usually means to cause death; here it is literal transport of a body.
explanation.definitionFit: The funeral vehicle that conveys a coffin to the burial, carrying the deceased away for the last time.

clue.text: Give out over time

indicators.note: turned over, so the word is read from back to front

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is handed out once the deadline has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over time' sounds like overtime or a period elapsing; 'over' is the signal to turn the following word around.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge light, heat, sound or gas, so it means to give out.

clue.text: Join drivers embracing very attractive switch to foreign team

indicators.note: something embracing another holds it within its arms

parts.note: the Automobile Association, the British motoring organisation for drivers

indicators.note: to switch things is to change them round, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: short for glamorous

indicators.note: foreign suggests something made strange, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer moves abroad, joining motorists who welcome the glamorous transfer to a foreign side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' and 'foreign' read as a football transfer, but each scrambles the word beside it. The AA is the Automobile Association, Britain's motoring breakdown club.
explanation.definitionFit: To amalgamate is to combine or merge separate things into one, which is to join them.

clue.text: Faithful foreign ally gains nothing

indicators.note: foreign suggests something made strange, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A dependable overseas partner gets nothing out of the arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal means steadfast in allegiance, which is what being faithful to a person or cause is.

clue.text: Ladies' fingers appear all right to painter

parts.note: OK means all right
Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A portrait painter is satisfied with how a woman's fingers look on canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' fingers' sounds like hands; it is the British name for the vegetable. RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra pods are long, slender and tapering, which is why the vegetable is also called lady's fingers.

clue.text: Split after holiday abroad?

parts.note: a short holiday is a break
being abroad is being away from home

explanation.surface: A couple part ways after a trip overseas, the question mark admitting the clue is playful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' reads as a break-up, which is the definition, not the Croatian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakaway is a separation from a larger body, such as a faction that splits from a party.

clue.text: Get one into a grave situation

definitions.text: Get one into a grave situation

parts.words: Get one into a grave situation
parts.note: surface reading: to land someone in serious trouble

parts.words: Get one into a grave situation
parts.note: setter's reading: to lay a body literally inside a burial pit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave situation' means a crisis, but read literally it is a hole in a cemetery.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a corpse, placing the dead person in a tomb or burial plot.

clue.text: Distress of man meeting couple

indicators.note: one piece meeting another touches it end to end

parts.note: Des, short for Desmond, a man's name
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: The anguish of a single man encountering a happy couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the complete loss of hope, an acute form of mental suffering or anguish.

clue.text: Family occupation at the time

indicators.note: one piece at another sits right beside it

parts.note: one's line of work is one's occupation
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A household's trade during the period in question.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is a person's ancestry or line of descent, the family they come from.
